# Tool reference

> Reference -- every MCP tool and prompt the server provides, and the CLI.

Every tool publishes the schema of its result, described under the tool and, for the result types tools share, in the last section. A tool that cannot do what was asked fails with an MCP tool error whose message says why. Connection, analysis and manipulation tools need a connected application (MuseScore, or experimentally Dorico); generation and rendering tools work on files.

## Connection tools

Connection tools: which application the server talks to.

Each application has its own connect and disconnect pair, and connecting
to one disconnects the other. The information and ping tools work with
whichever application is connected.

### `connect_to_musescore`

Connect to a running MuseScore Studio (4.4.2 or later).

The MCP Score Bridge plugin must be running in MuseScore with its
window open. Connecting disconnects any other application.
Negotiates the plugin protocol and returns supported commands and versions.
Receipt-capable plugins also return their session token and retention limits;
retain that token before calling execute_mutation_once.
Incompatible or legacy plugins must be reinstalled before connecting.

| Parameter | Type  | Default       | Description                          |
| --------- | ----- | ------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `host`    | `str` | `"localhost"` | WebSocket host (default: localhost). |
| `port`    | `int` | `8765`        | WebSocket port (default: 8765).      |

**Returns** `MuseScoreConnected`.

| Field         | Type                   | Description |
| ------------- | ---------------------- | ----------- |
| `application` | `str`                  |             |
| `uri`         | `str`                  |             |
| `bridge`      | `MuseScoreDiagnostics` |             |

### `disconnect_from_musescore`

Disconnect from MuseScore.

No parameters.

**Returns** `Disconnected`.

| Field         | Type  | Description |
| ------------- | ----- | ----------- |
| `application` | `str` |             |

### `connect_to_dorico`

Connect to a running Dorico via its Remote Control API (experimental).

Dorico support is experimental: the Remote Control API is undocumented,
command-only (it cannot read note content), and this bridge has not
been verified against a running Dorico. Dorico 4 and later serve the
API without a plugin; the port is set in Dorico's preferences.
Connecting disconnects any other application.

| Parameter | Type  | Default       | Description                                       |
| --------- | ----- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`    | `str` | `"localhost"` | WebSocket host (default: localhost).              |
| `port`    | `int` | `4560`        | WebSocket port (default: 4560, Dorico's default). |

**Returns** `Connected`.

| Field         | Type  | Description |
| ------------- | ----- | ----------- |
| `application` | `str` |             |
| `uri`         | `str` |             |

### `get_live_score_info`

Get information about the score open in MuseScore.

Title, parts, measure count and the opening key and time signatures.
Not available with Dorico, whose API cannot describe the score.

No parameters.

Requires an active MuseScore connection. Does not read or modify the score.

supported mutations and fixed limits; null requires an upgrade for receipts.

## Analysis tools

Read live musical contents independently of the application's cursor.

### `read_staff_context`

Read effective native staff context at passage start and observed changes.

Separate from event reads: no voice filtering, cursor creation or tempo query.
Direct native getters return instrument, raw clef/key codes, local meter,
time stretch and full chromatic/diatonic transposition on MuseScore 4.6+.
4.4 returns instrument-only observations with unavailable field reasons.
Position precision is native_fraction on 4.6+, native_integer_ticks on 4.4;
absolute_time and offset use whole notes, tick is supplementary integer data.
Meter spelling is preserved separately from actual pickup/irregular length.

Native segments are sampled within half-open measures, including changes
without notes in an otherwise empty voice. Unchanged samples are coalesced.
sampling_complete confirms traversal of bounded samples, not full context
fidelity. Missing getters return null plus reasons. Tempo, custom key notation,
written pitch/octave and displayed measure labels remain unsupported.
No guessing key modes/names or toggling concert pitch. No score revision or
identity guarantees. Maximum 64 measures, 4096 staff-by-point samples and
bounded traversal; excess requests fail without partial timelines. Not Dorico.

| Parameter       | Type          | Default    | Description                                                      |
| --------------- | ------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `start_measure` | `int`         | (required) | First ordinal measure (1-indexed, inclusive).                    |
| `end_measure`   | `int`         | (required) | Last ordinal measure (1-indexed, inclusive).                     |
| `staff`         | `int \| None` | `None`     | Zero-based staff index; omit to query every staff independently. |

**Returns** `StaffContext`.

| Field                  | Type                                          | Description                                                              |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `source`               | `str`                                         |                                                                          |
| `start_measure`        | `int`                                         |                                                                          |
| `end_measure`          | `int`                                         |                                                                          |
| `staves`               | `list[int]`                                   |                                                                          |
| `native_major_version` | `int`                                         |                                                                          |
| `native_minor_version` | `int`                                         |                                                                          |
| `position_precision`   | `"native_fraction" \| "native_integer_ticks"` |                                                                          |
| `sampling`             | `str`                                         |                                                                          |
| `sampling_complete`    | `bool`                                        | All bounded samples traversed; does not establish full context fidelity. |
| `tempo_status`         | `str`                                         |                                                                          |
| `sampled_point_count`  | `int`                                         |                                                                          |
| `staff_point_queries`  | `int`                                         |                                                                          |
| `timelines`            | `list[StaffTimeline]`                         |                                                                          |
| `limitations`          | `list[str]`                                   |                                                                          |

### `read_passage`

Read every rhythmic event in an inclusive range of live MuseScore measures.

Returns chords, rests, concert pitch names, exact offsets and durations
across all requested staves and voices, including unsaved changes. Does
not move the selection or the bridge's logical cursor. Other segment
elements and annotations include their type and text where available.
Chord/rest lyrics include native text, zero-based verse, syllabic and
placement codes/names; null means unavailable, [] means no attached lyrics.
Chord articulations include native symbol IDs and localized names where
supported (MuseScore 4.6+); older wrappers report null, not an empty list.
The result lists notation details not yet serialized in `unsupported`;
`range_complete` describes traversal, not full notation fidelity.
Oversize reads fail without returning a truncated passage; request a
smaller range. Not available with Dorico or an older MuseScore plugin.

| Parameter       | Type          | Default    | Description                                              |
| --------------- | ------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `start_measure` | `int`         | (required) | First ordinal measure (1-indexed, repeats not expanded). |
| `end_measure`   | `int`         | (required) | Last ordinal measure (inclusive, 1-indexed).             |
| `staff`         | `int \| None` | `None`     | Staff index (0-indexed). Omit to read all staves.        |
| `voice`         | `int \| None` | `None`     | Voice index (0-3). Omit to read all voices.              |

**Returns** `Passage`: Live events across an inclusive measure range, without moving selection.

| Field            | Type                   | Description                                                                |
| ---------------- | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `source`         | `str`                  |                                                                            |
| `start_measure`  | `int`                  |                                                                            |
| `end_measure`    | `int`                  |                                                                            |
| `staves`         | `list[int]`            |                                                                            |
| `voices`         | `list[int]`            |                                                                            |
| `measures`       | `list[PassageMeasure]` |                                                                            |
| `range_complete` | `bool`                 | Whether every requested measure and rhythmic event was traversed.          |
| `unsupported`    | `list[str]`            | Notation details not serialized, even when the rhythmic range is complete. |

| `staff`   | `int \| None` | `None`     | Staff index (0-indexed). Omit to read all staves.         |
| `voice`   | `int \| None` | `None`     | Voice index (0-3). Omit to read all voices.               |

**Returns** `Passage`: Live events across an inclusive measure range, without moving selection.

| Field            | Type                   | Description                                                                |
| ---------------- | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| `unsupported`    | `list[str]`            | Notation details not serialized, even when the rhythmic range is complete. |

### `get_event_at_position`

Read the chord or rest starting at an exact live MuseScore position.

All position coordinates are explicit. Offsets are exact fractions of a
whole note: 1/2 selects an onset halfway through a whole note, not beat 2.
Equivalent fractions select the same onset. A position inside a sustained
event does not match. Non-rhythmic annotations are excluded, and ambiguous
onsets are rejected. Uses one live passage read without moving selection
or the bridge cursor, including unsaved changes.

Omitting note_index returns the entire event; supplying it also returns
that tone from the event's current notes list. Indices are ephemeral
ordering within this response. The result preserves the passage reader's
unsupported notation list. It provides no stable event ID, score identity,
revision token, or guarantee that the address remains valid for an edit.

| Parameter            | Type          | Default    | Description                                                                                   |
| -------------------- | ------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `measure`            | `int`         | (required) | Ordinal measure (integer >= 1; repeats not expanded).                                         |
| `staff`              | `int`         | (required) | Staff index (integer >= 0).                                                                   |
| `voice`              | `int`         | (required) | Voice index (integer from 0 through 3).                                                       |
| `offset_numerator`   | `int`         | (required) | Whole-note onset fraction numerator (integer >= 0).                                           |
| `offset_denominator` | `int`         | (required) | Whole-note onset fraction denominator (integer > 0).                                          |
| `note_index`         | `int \| None` | `None`     | Index into the returned chord's notes (integer >= 0). Omit to select the whole chord or rest. |

**Returns** `LocatedEvent`: A current rhythmic event, without durable identity or edit preconditions.

| Field         | Type                  | Description                                                           |
| ------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `source`      | `str`                 |                                                                       |
| `scope`       | `str`                 | The address and note index describe only the returned live snapshot.  |
| `address`     | `EventAddress`        | Requested address with its whole-note offset reduced to lowest terms. |
| `event`       | `PassageEvent`        | The entire chord or rest, including all chord tones.                  |
| `note`        | `PassageNote \| None` | The selected tone, or null when the whole event was requested.        |
| `unsupported` | `list[str]`           | Notation details omitted by the underlying live passage reader.       |

### `get_selection_properties`

Get properties of the current selection in the connected application.

MuseScore reports its bridge logical cursor (not the actual UI selection);
use read_current_selection for selected native elements and contents.
Dorico reports the names, types and values of every property of the
selected items, which is the closest its API gets to reading the score.

No parameters.

**Returns** `SelectionProperties`: What the application reports about the current selection.

MuseScore reports the bridge logical cursor; Dorico reports the properties
of the selected items as they come from its API.

| Field        | Type                       | Description |
| ------------ | -------------------------- | ----------- |
| `cursor`     | `CursorInfo \| None`       |             |
| `properties` | `ApplicationReply \| None` |             |
| `warning`    | `str \| None`              |             |

### `read_current_selection`

Read the actual MuseScore UI selection, including unsaved selected contents.

Returns an empty, distinct-element, or range selection from the native list.
Range bounds are half-open; a null end tick means score end. The native
list respects current selection filters; filter settings themselves are
unavailable. It is never expanded to all events inside the bounding range.
Selected notes are distinct from whole chords: event_context contains the
owner chord, but only note/note_index identify the selected tone. Indices
belong only to this snapshot. Ordinary segment-bound notes/chords/rests
reuse passage contents, including available lyrics/articulations. Other
types are opaque descriptors and may lack content or exact positions;
grace-note positions and persistent identities are unsupported.
Does not navigate, select, export, or create undo commands. The bridge's
logical cursor is independent of this actual UI selection. Not Dorico.

No parameters.

**Returns** `CurrentSelection`: A single synchronous read of the actual native GUI selection.

| Field               | Type                          | Description                                                                |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `source`            | `str`                         |                                                                            |
| `kind`              | `"none" \| "list" \| "range"` |                                                                            |
| `range`             | `SelectionRange \| None`      |                                                                            |
| `elements`          | `list[SelectionItem]`         |                                                                            |
| `elements_complete` | `bool`                        | Every native selected-list entry was returned; not full notation fidelity. |
| `observed_voices`   | `list[int]`                   | Voices encountered in selected tracks, not the configured voice filter.    |
| `filter_state`      | `str`                         |                                                                            |
| `unsupported`       | `list[str]`                   |                                                                            |

## Manipulation tools

Manipulation tools: change the score in the connected application.

Legacy edits navigate to a measure first. Guarded pitch edits instead resolve
an explicit position and validate its expected contents atomically in the plugin.
Unsupported operations return the application's own explanation:
Dorico's Remote Control API triggers commands but cannot type into
popovers or move the selection, so most of these tools work with MuseScore
only.

### `add_live_note`

Add a note at the start of a measure in the live score.

Consecutive calls on the same measure append notes one after another,
since the application advances its cursor after each note. Not
available with Dorico.

| Parameter     | Type  | Default    | Description                                                        |
| ------------- | ----- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `measure`     | `int` | (required) | Measure number (1-indexed).                                        |
| `pitch`       | `int` | (required) | MIDI pitch (60 = middle C).                                        |
| `numerator`   | `int` | `1`        | Duration numerator (default 1, with denominator 4 = quarter note). |
| `denominator` | `int` | `4`        | Duration denominator (default 4).                                  |
| `staff`       | `int` | `0`        | Staff index (0-indexed, default: 0).                               |

**Returns** `NoteAdded`: A note was added; the position is where the cursor went afterwards.

| Field      | Type       | Description                 |
| ---------- | ---------- | --------------------------- |
| `measure`  | `int`      | Measure number (1-indexed). |
| `staff`    | `int`      | Staff index (0-indexed).    |
| `pitch`    | `int`      |                             |
| `duration` | `Duration` |                             |

### `add_live_chord_tone`

Match a complete live chord snapshot and add one ordinary sounding tone.

All exposed expected metadata is required and compared, including nullable
text/lyrics/articulations. Existing notes, rhythm and exposed metadata are
preserved; duplicate sounding pitches and inconsistent native transposition
intervals reject before mutation. Written TPC derives from unanimous native
peer intervals, without a written-octave guess or concert-mode change.
One native undo command; no navigation or automatic replay. Known-open
command cancellation is verified by a fresh full target snapshot. Commit
uncertainty is unknown; known committed failures are applied_unverified.
UI selection/layout are not preserved; logical cursor is untouched. Scope
is target contents, without score identity, revision or non-target claims.
Use execute_mutation_once kind add_chord_tone for duplicate protection;
this direct tool has none. Not available with Dorico.

| Parameter  | Type                | Default    | Description                                                 |
| ---------- | ------------------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `measure`  | `int`               | (required) | Ordinal measure (1-indexed).                                |
| `staff`    | `int`               | (required) | Staff index (0-indexed).                                    |
| `voice`    | `int`               | (required) | Voice index (0-3).                                          |
| `offset`   | `WholeNoteFraction` | (required) | Exact onset as a whole-note fraction.                       |
| `pitch`    | `int`               | (required) | New sounding MIDI pitch (0-127).                            |
| `tpc`      | `int`               | (required) | Concert spelling (-1 to 33), consistent with pitch.         |
| `expected` | `ChordToneSnapshot` | (required) | Complete fresh live chord event, with all exposed metadata. |

**Returns** `ChordToneEdit`: Actual target snapshots; indices are ephemeral within this operation.

| Field               | Type                | Description |
| ------------------- | ------------------- | ----------- |
| `operation`         | `"add" \| "remove"` |             |
| `measure`           | `int`               |             |
| `note_index_before` | `int \| None`       |             |
| `note_index_after`  | `int \| None`       |             |
| `before`            | `PassageEvent`      |             |
| `after`             | `PassageEvent`      |             |
| `verified`          | `bool`              |             |
| `mutation_status`   | `str`               |             |
| `snapshot_scope`    | `str`               |             |
| `selection_status`  | `str`               |             |
| `limitations`       | `list[str]`         |             |

### `remove_live_chord_tone`

Match a complete live chord snapshot and remove one tone, retaining rhythm.

Requires at least two tones and the ordinary pitched-chord eligibility of
guarded pitch edits. The removed tone must have verified empty native child
and spanner lists; missing metadata rejects (MuseScore 4.4 cannot remove).
The selected wrapper is never accessed after deletion; verification and
rollback use freshly resolved native contents. All exposed expected fields
are required and compared; surviving notes, lyrics and articulations remain.
One native undo step. Cancellation only affects its known open command and
rolled_back requires a full target reread; uncertain commit is unknown and
known committed verification failures remain applied_unverified. No global
undo, automatic replay, sequence embedding, score identity or revision claim.
UI selection/layout are not preserved; logical cursor is untouched. Use
execute_mutation_once kind remove_chord_tone for caller-retained duplicate
protection; this direct tool has none. Not available with Dorico.

| Parameter    | Type                | Default    | Description                                                 |
| ------------ | ------------------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `measure`    | `int`               | (required) | Ordinal measure (1-indexed).                                |
| `staff`      | `int`               | (required) | Staff index (0-indexed).                                    |
| `voice`      | `int`               | (required) | Voice index (0-3).                                          |
| `offset`     | `WholeNoteFraction` | (required) | Exact onset as a whole-note fraction.                       |
| `note_index` | `int`               | (required) | Ephemeral tone index in the complete expected snapshot.     |
| `expected`   | `ChordToneSnapshot` | (required) | Complete fresh live chord event, with all exposed metadata. |

**Returns** `ChordToneEdit`: Actual target snapshots; indices are ephemeral within this operation.

| Field               | Type                | Description |

### `set_live_note_pitch`

Match a live chord snapshot and change one tone's concert pitch and spelling.

Pass the complete chord event from a fresh live read as `expected`, including
every tone's written_tpc. The plugin checks the onset, track, rhythm, pitches,
and spellings in the same synchronous handler as the edit. A mismatch rejects
the edit without opening an undo step. Successful edits return actual native
before/after events and create one undo step; no-op requests create none.
Chord-tone indices belong only to that snapshot, not to later reads.
Lyrics and articulations in the snapshot are accepted as informational
metadata; the pitch guard does not compare them or protect their changes.

This guards only the target chord, not a score identity or global revision;
switching to another score with identical target contents is not detected.
Tied, grace, tuplet, drum, tablature, duplicate-tone and microtonal targets are
rejected. Written octave is not returned. Not available with Dorico.

| Parameter    | Type                | Default    | Description                                                         |
| ------------ | ------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `measure`    | `int`               | (required) | Ordinal measure (1-indexed, repeats not expanded).                  |
| `staff`      | `int`               | (required) | Explicit staff index (0-indexed).                                   |
| `voice`      | `int`               | (required) | Explicit voice index (0-3).                                         |
| `offset`     | `WholeNoteFraction` | (required) | Exact onset within the measure, as a whole-note fraction.           |
| `note_index` | `int`               | (required) | Tone index in expected.notes (0-indexed, snapshot-local).           |
| `pitch`      | `int`               | (required) | Replacement sounding MIDI pitch (0-127; 60 is middle C).            |
| `tpc`        | `int`               | (required) | Replacement concert tonal pitch class (-1 to 33); must match pitch. |
| `expected`   | `ExpectedChord`     | (required) | Complete live chord event, with written_tpc for every tone.         |

**Returns** `PitchEdit`: Actual before/after notation, read inside the synchronous edit handler.

| Field               | Type                       | Description                                                               |
| ------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `measure`           | `int`                      |                                                                           |
| `note_index_before` | `int`                      | Ephemeral chord-tone index in the required expected snapshot.             |
| `note_index_after`  | `int`                      | Index after editing; a later operation must take a fresh snapshot.        |
| `before`            | `PassageEvent`             |                                                                           |
| `after`             | `PassageEvent`             |                                                                           |
| `verified`          | `bool`                     |                                                                           |
| `mutation_status`   | `"applied" \| "unchanged"` |                                                                           |
| `snapshot_scope`    | `str`                      |                                                                           |
| `limitations`       | `list[str]`                | Target matching does not establish application-wide identity or revision. |

### `set_live_note_pitches`

Preflight up to 32 independent chord targets, then edit in one undo command.

Every target uses the existing strict guarded pitch request and a complete
fresh chord snapshot. Chords must be distinct, even for different tone
indices or equivalent onset fractions. All snapshots, spelling and native
eligibility are checked before any write. No navigation or dependent steps.
An all-no-op batch creates no undo command. Writes verify actual target
pitches, peers, rhythm and fresh exposed metadata, including lyrics and
articulations. Expected attachment metadata remains informational.
Only a known open command can be cancelled; rolled_back requires re-reading
ALL exposed target snapshots. Commit uncertainty is unknown; postcommit
failures are applied_unverified. Global undo is never invoked automatically.
Scope is target chords, not score identity/revision or non-target contents.
No automatic mutation replay. Use execute_mutation_once with kind
set_note_pitches for caller-retained duplicate protection; this direct tool
has none. Not available with Dorico or an older plugin lacking setNotePitches.

| Parameter | Type                     | Default    | Description                                                     |
| --------- | ------------------------ | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `edits`   | `list[PitchEditRequest]` | (required) | One through 32 strict pitch requests targeting distinct chords. |

**Returns** `PitchBatchEdit`: Actual native snapshots for every target, in request order.

| Field             | Type                       | Description |
| ----------------- | -------------------------- | ----------- |
| `edits`           | `list[PitchEdit]`          |             |
| `verified`        | `bool`                     |             |
| `mutation_status` | `"applied" \| "unchanged"` |             |
| `snapshot_scope`  | `str`                      |             |
| `limitations`     | `list[str]`                |             |

### `set_live_event_duration`

Change an ordinary live chord's duration under an explicit rest policy.

Pass ALL events from a fresh get_measure_content read filtered to the explicit staff
and voice as expected. This complete voice-measure snapshot is checked inside
the synchronous native handler before any mutation. Default shorten_fill_rest
shortens and fills released time. Explicit extend_into_rests lengthens only
through complete contiguous plain rests in the same voice and bar, ending
exactly at a rest boundary. Notes, gaps, partial rests, attached/hidden/cross-staff
rests and unknown eligibility reject before mutation. Only undotted whole through
32nd durations are accepted. MuseScore 4.7+ (major version 4) is required for
native duration rewriting and spanner inspection; older versions reject.

Target attachments (including lyrics/articulations), beams, ties, tuplets,
grace notes, drum/tab staves, microtonality and intersecting or unknown score
spanners reject. Distant spanner time/track metadata is verified unchanged.
Successful edits return actual before/after events across ALL measure tracks,
checking neighboring events and spelling, and create one undo step. No-op
requests create none. Selection/layout may change; logical cursor is untouched.
This snapshot does not identify a score instance or global revision and cannot
detect switching to identical contents. Not available with Dorico.
Extension requires the separately advertised extendEventDuration command;
an older shortening-only plugin rejects before send. Neither duration policy
supports mutation receipts or sequence execution; transport loss is not replayed.

| Parameter  | Type                                         | Default               | Description                                                        |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |

## Note_rest tools

Guarded time-preserving rest/note replacement in the live application.

### `fill_live_rest`

Replace a plain rest onset with one pitched note, leaving trailing rests.

MuseScore 4.7+ in major version 4 only. Pass ALL fresh get_measure_content
events filtered to the explicit staff and voice as expected. This snapshot
is matched atomically before any mutation. A canonical undotted whole through
32nd note must fit entirely in the original rest and bar. Ordinary full-measure
rests require a regular 4/4 bar; pickups and irregular full-measure rests reject.
No occupied time is overwritten or shifted. Native suffix rests may be dotted
or split; their exact contiguous coverage is verified, with other measure
tracks, adjacent measure events, exposed context and spanner metadata.

Pitch is concert MIDI; tpc is concert spelling (C=14, F#=20). Native staff
transposition supplies written TPC without changing the score display mode.
Dotted targets, beams, attachments, tuplets, ties, grace notes, microtonality,
drum/tab, nonunit time stretch and intersecting/unknown spanners reject.
Actual before/after all-track measure events are returned after one undo step.
UI selection/layout may change; the logical bridge cursor stays put. Snapshot
coverage is exposed notation, not full engraving or score identity/revision;
identical contents in another score cannot be distinguished. Not available
with Dorico. No sequence or mutation-receipt support; never automatically
retry this mutation after an uncertain response.

| Parameter  | Type                          | Default    | Description |
| ---------- | ----------------------------- | ---------- | ----------- |
| `measure`  | `int`                         | (required) |             |
| `staff`    | `int`                         | (required) |             |
| `voice`    | `int`                         | (required) |             |
| `offset`   | `WholeNoteFraction`           | (required) |             |
| `duration` | `WholeNoteFraction`           | (required) |             |
| `pitch`    | `int`                         | (required) |             |
| `tpc`      | `int`                         | (required) |             |
| `expected` | `list[ExpectedDurationEvent]` | (required) |             |

**Returns** `NoteRestEdit`: Actual all-track measure events, reread after structural replacement.

| Field              | Type                 | Description |
| ------------------ | -------------------- | ----------- |
| `measure`          | `int`                |             |
| `staff`            | `int`                |             |
| `voice`            | `int`                |             |
| `before`           | `list[PassageEvent]` |             |
| `after`            | `list[PassageEvent]` |             |
| `verified`         | `bool`               |             |
| `mutation_status`  | `str`                |             |
| `snapshot_scope`   | `str`                |             |
| `selection_status` | `str`                |             |
| `limitations`      | `list[str]`          |             |

### `replace_live_note_with_rest`

Replace an ordinary single-tone chord with equal-duration plain rest coverage.

Native rhythmic decomposition may split rests; their exact interval union
must equal the original chord span. Supply ALL fresh target staff/voice
measure events as expected. Atomic native
validation and actual all-track read-back prevent partial or stale replacement.
Only undotted whole through 32nd, ordinary unbeamed single-tone chords without
lyrics, articulations, other attachments, ties, tuplets, grace notes,
microtonality or intersecting/unknown spanners are supported. Requires
MuseScore 4.7+ in major version 4 and pitched non-drum/non-tab staff with unit
time stretch. Other events, adjacent measures, exposed context and spanner
metadata are verified unchanged. One undo step, no time shifting. UI selection
and layout may change; logical bridge cursor is untouched. No app-wide score
identity/revision or full engraving guarantee. No Dorico, sequence, mutation
receipts or automatic replay; inspect an uncertain response before proceeding.

| Parameter  | Type                          | Default    | Description |
| ---------- | ----------------------------- | ---------- | ----------- |
| `measure`  | `int`                         | (required) |             |
| `staff`    | `int`                         | (required) |             |
| `voice`    | `int`                         | (required) |             |
| `offset`   | `WholeNoteFraction`           | (required) |             |
| `expected` | `list[ExpectedDurationEvent]` | (required) |             |

**Returns** `NoteRestEdit`: Actual all-track measure events, reread after structural replacement.

| Field              | Type                 | Description |
| ------------------ | -------------------- | ----------- |
| `measure`          | `int`                |             |
| `staff`            | `int`                |             |
| `voice`            | `int`                |             |
| `before`           | `list[PassageEvent]` |             |
| `after`            | `list[PassageEvent]` |             |
| `verified`         | `bool`               |             |
| `mutation_status`  | `str`                |             |
| `snapshot_scope`   | `str`                |             |
| `selection_status` | `str`                |             |
| `limitations`      | `list[str]`          |             |

## Receipts tools

Execute explicitly identified guarded mutations and retrieve their history.

### `execute_mutation_once`

Execute one supported guarded mutation with a caller-retained ID.

Create and retain a unique operation_id BEFORE the first call. Obtain the
plugin session from connect_to_musescore/get_musescore_bridge_info. Repeating
the identical ID, session and complete payload returns retained history;
changing the payload conflicts. This command is never automatically replayed.
After a lost response or cancellation, explicitly retry the exact request or
read its receipt. Never replace the session token automatically after restart.
Supported kinds: set_note_pitch, set_note_pitches, add_chord_tone and
remove_chord_tone. The matching native command must be advertised; older
plugins reject unsupported kinds before sending. Direct mutation tools are
not protected. Batch targets must be distinct chords, at most 32.

Receipt completion means an original native reply was retained, including
errors; it does not mean the edit succeeded. Replies are HISTORICAL, including
after undo or further edits, and are not verification of current score state.
Pending/unknown IDs remain reserved. The bounded non-evicting ledger lasts
only for that plugin instance. Native score identity is not established.

| Parameter                 | Type                                                                                                                 | Default    | Description |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ----------- |
| `operation_id`            | `str`                                                                                                                | (required) |             |
| `expected_plugin_session` | `str`                                                                                                                | (required) |             |
| `mutation`                | `GuardedPitchMutation \| GuardedPitchBatchMutation \| GuardedAddChordToneMutation \| GuardedRemoveChordToneMutation` | (required) |             |

**Returns** `MutationReceipt`: Retained operation history, never a verification of the current score.

| Field            | Type                                                                                | Description                                                                  |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `plugin_session` | `str`                                                                               |                                                                              |
| `operation_id`   | `str`                                                                               |                                                                              |
| `status`         | `"not_found" \| "pending" \| "completed" \| "unknown"`                              |                                                                              |
| `command`        | `"setNotePitch" \| "setNotePitches" \| "addChordTone" \| "removeChordTone" \| None` |                                                                              |
| `cached`         | `bool`                                                                              | Lookup/retrieval response, not proof that an operation completed or applied. |
| `historical`     | `bool`                                                                              |                                                                              |
| `original_reply` | `dict \| None`                                                                      | Original native JSON fields, including errors, preserved in native casing.   |
| `reason`         | `str \| None`                                                                       | Bounded cause for an unknown receipt; no automatic retry is implied.         |

### `read_mutation_receipt`

Read retained operation history from the SAME plugin instance.

Not-found means no reservation exists at observation time; an earlier queued
request may still arrive. It does not authorize a new ID or prove no effect.
A restarted plugin rejects the old session rather than reporting not-found.
Stored replies are historical, not the current score. Lookup never executes
a mutation and remains available when the non-evicting ledger is full.

| Parameter                 | Type  | Default    | Description |
| ------------------------- | ----- | ---------- | ----------- |
| `operation_id`            | `str` | (required) |             |
| `expected_plugin_session` | `str` | (required) |             |

**Returns** `MutationReceipt`: Retained operation history, never a verification of the current score.

| Field            | Type                                                                                | Description                                                                  |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `plugin_session` | `str`                                                                               |                                                                              |
| `operation_id`   | `str`                                                                               |                                                                              |
| `status`         | `"not_found" \| "pending" \| "completed" \| "unknown"`                              |                                                                              |
| `command`        | `"setNotePitch" \| "setNotePitches" \| "addChordTone" \| "removeChordTone" \| None` |                                                                              |
| `cached`         | `bool`                                                                              | Lookup/retrieval response, not proof that an operation completed or applied. |
| `historical`     | `bool`                                                                              |                                                                              |
| `original_reply` | `dict \| None`                                                                      | Original native JSON fields, including errors, preserved in native casing.   |
| `reason`         | `str \| None`                                                                       | Bounded cause for an unknown receipt; no automatic retry is implied.         |

## Generate tools

Generation tools — run music21 scripts and serve the score-generate guide.

These make score generation available in any MCP client, not only Claude
Code (where the bundled `score-generate` skill covers the same job).

### `generate_score`

Run a music21 Python script to generate a score file (MusicXML).

Write a COMPLETE, self-contained music21 script that builds the whole
score and ends by exporting it, e.g.
`score.write("musicxml", fp="My Piece.musicxml")`. Use a plain file
name (no directory) so the file lands in the working directory and is
reported back in `output_files`. Read the `score_generation_guide`
tool first: it holds the music21 conventions this project relies on
(flats are written `B-` not `Bb`, metadata, repeats, volta brackets,
transposing instruments, and a full template).

The script runs on the user's machine with the user's privileges, in the
same Python interpreter as this server (so music21 is importable).
Only send code the user would be comfortable running themselves.

| Parameter    | Type          | Default    | Description                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------ | ------------- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `script`     | `str`         | (required) | Complete Python source of the generation script.                                                                                                                  |
| `output_dir` | `str \| None` | `None`     | Working directory for the run. Defaults to a fresh directory under the user's Desktop (or home directory when there is no Desktop). Created if it does not exist. |
| `timeout`    | `float`       | `120.0`    | Seconds to wait before killing the script (default: 120).                                                                                                         |

A script that fails is a tool error whose message ends with the last
lines of its stderr.

**Returns** `GeneratedScore`.

| Field          | Type        | Description                                                              |
| -------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `output_files` | `list[str]` | Absolute paths of the files the script created in its working directory. |
| `stdout`       | `str`       |                                                                          |

### `score_generation_guide`

Return the score generation guide for writing music21 scripts.

Read this before calling `generate_score`. It is the bundled
`score-generate` skill (instructions, music21 conventions and
troubleshooting), the instrument class reference (which class to use for
each instrument, with transposition handled by music21), and a complete
runnable template script. Takes no parameters.

Returns the guide as Markdown.

No parameters.

**Returns** `str`.

### Prompt `score-generate`

Load the score-generate instructions (music21 conventions, instrument reference and template) before generating a score with generate_score.

## Render tools

Rendering tools: export score files through the MuseScore command line.

### `render_score`

Render a score file to PDF, PNG, MIDI, MP3, WAV or MusicXML.

Runs the MuseScore Studio 4 command line, so MuseScore Studio 4 must be
installed. It does not need to be running, and no plugin or live
connection is required. The input is typically a MusicXML file
(.musicxml, .xml, .mxl) but can be any file MuseScore opens, such as
.mscz or .mid.

MuseScore is located from the MCP_SCORE_MUSESCORE_PATH environment
variable, then PATH (mscore, musescore, mscore4portable, MuseScore4),
then the platform default install location (macOS app bundle, Windows
Program Files, Linux Flatpak). If it is not found automatically, set
MCP_SCORE_MUSESCORE_PATH to the executable in the MCP server's
environment.

| Parameter     | Type          | Default    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------- | ------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `input_path`  | `str`         | (required) | Path to the score file to render.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `format`      | `str`         | `"pdf"`    | One of "pdf", "png", "midi", "mp3", "wav", "musicxml" (default: pdf). PNG export writes one file per page, named with a -1, -2, ... suffix before the extension.                                                      |
| `output_path` | `str \| None` | `None`     | Where to write the result. Defaults to the input path with the format's extension. Its extension must match the format, its directory must exist, and it must not be the input file. An existing file is overwritten. |

**Returns** `RenderedScore`.

| Field          | Type          | Description                                                              |
| -------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `output_path`  | `str`         | The file MuseScore was asked to write.                                   |
| `output_files` | `list[str]`   | The files it wrote: one, or one per page for PNG.                        |
| `format`       | `str`         |                                                                          |
| `warning`      | `str \| None` | Set when MuseScore wrote the output but did not exit cleanly afterwards. |

A native chord articulation; null fields are unavailable.

| Field            | Type                         | Description                                                              |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `symbol`         | `int \| None`                | Native SymId code, scoped to the application's version, not an event ID. |
| `name`           | `str \| None`                | Native localized subtype name; not a stable machine-readable identifier. |
| `placement`      | `int \| None`                | Native placement property, not the final geometric engraving position.   |
| `placement_name` | `"ABOVE" \| "BELOW" \| None` |                                                                          |
| `anchor`         | `int \| None`                | Native articulation-anchor enum code, where available.                   |
| `direction`      | `int \| None`                | Native direction enum code, where available.                             |

### `PassageEvent`

An element at an exact position in the live score.

| Field             | Type                                | Description                                                                   |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kind`            | `"chord" \| "rest" \| "other"`      |                                                                               |
| `type`            | `int`                               | MuseScore's element type code.                                                |
| `staff`           | `int`                               | Staff index, starting at zero.                                                |
| `voice`           | `int`                               | Voice index, starting at zero.                                                |
| `tick`            | `int`                               |                                                                               |
| `offset`          | `Duration`                          | Exact offset from the measure start, as a fraction of a whole note.           |
| `duration`        | `Duration \| None`                  | Notated length, including dots; null for non-rhythmic elements.               |
| `actual_duration` | `Duration \| None`                  | Elapsed score time, including tuplet scaling; null when unavailable.          |
| `notes`           | `list[PassageNote]`                 |                                                                               |
| `text`            | `str \| None`                       | Text of an annotation, where exposed by MuseScore.                            |
| `lyrics`          | `list[PassageLyric] \| None`        | Native chord/rest lyrics; [] means none, null means unavailable/inapplicable. |
| `articulations`   | `list[PassageArticulation] \| None` | Chord articulations; [] means none, null means unavailable/inapplicable.      |

### `PassageLyric`

One native lyric attached to a chord/rest; null fields are unavailable.

| Field            | Type                                               | Description                                                            |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `text`           | `str \| None`                                      | Native text, including any MuseScore rich-text markup; not normalized. |
| `verse`          | `int \| None`                                      | Native zero-based verse index, not a displayed verse label.            |
| `syllabic`       | `int \| None`                                      | Native syllabic enum code, retained even when its name is unknown.     |
| `syllabic_name`  | `"SINGLE" \| "BEGIN" \| "END" \| "MIDDLE" \| None` |                                                                        |
| `placement`      | `int \| None`                                      | Native placement enum code, not a geometric layout coordinate.         |
| `placement_name` | `"ABOVE" \| "BELOW" \| None`                       |                                                                        |

### `PassageMeasure`

One measure across the requested staves and voices.

| Field             | Type                    | Description                                                               |
| ----------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `measure`         | `int`                   | Ordinal measure number, starting at one, without expanding repeats.       |
| `tick`            | `int`                   | Absolute measure start in MuseScore ticks.                                |
| `actual_duration` | `Duration \| None`      | Actual measure length, as a fraction of a whole note (including pickups). |
| `time_signature`  | `TimeSignature \| None` | Nominal meter, where exposed; never inferred from the measure length.     |
| `events`          | `list[PassageEvent]`    |                                                                           |

### `PassageNote`

A chord tone, with concert pitch spelling independent of display mode.

| Field           | Type          | Description                                                           |
| --------------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pitch`         | `int`         | Sounding MIDI pitch; 60 is middle C.                                  |
| `tpc`           | `int`         | Concert tonal pitch class (MuseScore tpc1).                           |
| `name`          | `str`         | Concert spelling and octave, for example C#4 or Db4.                  |
| `written_tpc`   | `int \| None` | Written TPC (tpc2), without octave; null on older plugins.            |
| `displayed_tpc` | `int`         | TPC in the current concert/transposed display mode; not a MIDI pitch. |

## CLI

```
usage: mcp-score [-h] <command> ...

MCP server for music notation; runs the server by default.

positional arguments:
  <command>
    serve           run the MCP server (the default)
    run             run a Python script with music21 available; extra
                    arguments go to it
    install         install the skill and the MuseScore plugin
    install-skill   install the score-generate skill for Claude Code
    install-plugin  install the bridge plugin into MuseScore

options:
  -h, --help        show this help message and exit
```
